---
title: "Optimal reports along the criterion-weight path"
subtitle: "4.4 · after the postrank theory book, chapter 11"
description: "Exact weight intervals and criterion-specific errors of minimum-risk reports."
---

With two criteria, the risk of a fixed report varies affinely with the error weight. The lower envelope identifies
the report or reports with minimum weighted risk at each weight, including the common withholding charge. The path
is calculated from these functions rather than inferred from a sampled slider grid. Step charts record the
criterion-specific expected wrong shares and disclosure, while the risk lines explain the change points. Each
interval retains a fixed report, although its weighted risk continues to vary. Boundary solutions are evaluated
separately where several reports may be optimal.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Equal weights.** The selected report states 9 pairs. Its expected wrong shares are .0177 on score A and .0267 on score B. The interval table and lower envelope identify the weights for which this report is optimal.
- **Lower A weight.** The best report states 12 pairs and favours score B's ordering of the conflicting sites. Both criterion shares stay constant through the interior of its interval, although the weighted risk changes.
- **Higher A weight.** The report again states 12 pairs, with {A, B} > {C, D} > {E, F}. Its expected wrong share on score B is .237. Equal disclosure does not mean equal pair relations.
- **Score B only.** At the endpoint, 2 reports share the smallest risk. The expected wrong shares on score A are .200 and .215. The boundary table keeps their identities and differing profiles, including the tiny first interval.
- **No cap.** The unrestricted calculation searches all 4,683 reports. The current equal-weight report still states 9 pairs, but the complete path can differ away from the selected weight.
- **Higher withholding cost.** The uncapped current report states 14 pairs. The interval table retains every short interval; both criterion-share paths use these same boundaries.

::: {.callout-note}
The path uses the six fictional sites' declared independent normal posteriors. Each exact boundary can have several best reports; the table solves the boundary itself and states the equal-risk tolerance. A zero-width endpoint entry and a tiny positive interval remain visible in the table even when a screen cannot give them a visible width. Risks at different weights correspond to different losses, so a falling line is not an improvement under one fixed objective. The largest lower-envelope risk is a risk value, while its location is a weight.
:::

Standalone: [weight-path](../../embed/weight-path.html), for example `?w=.5&tau=.2&cap=3`.
